label: House or first name, regnal, plain
summary: A text naming the character by a titled house name or else the first name, without a tooltip, with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only: the parts are 'titled house name or first name', 'no tooltip' and 'regnal' (a ruler's number such as the second). Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House or first name or me
summary: A text naming the character by a titled house name or else the first name, or a first-person word for the viewer.
details: Going by its name only (the 'OrMe' part). Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House/first name or me, plain
summary: The 'titled house name, first name or me' text for the character, without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only: the same as GetTitledHouseNameOrFirstNameOrMe, with 'NoTooltip' added. Vanilla never uses it.

label: House/first name or me, regnal plain
summary: The 'titled house name, first name or me' text for the character, without a tooltip and with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House/first name or me, regnal
summary: The 'titled house name, first name or me' text for the character, with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Titled house or first name, possessive
summary: The character's titled house name or else first name, in the possessive form (as in 'Karl's').
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House or first name possessive, plain
summary: The possessive 'titled house name or first name' text, without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House/first name possessive, regnal plain
summary: The possessive 'titled house name or first name' text, without a tooltip and with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House/first name, possessive, my
summary: The possessive 'titled house name or first name' text, or a first-person 'my' form.
details: Going by its name only (the 'OrMy' part). Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House/first name, my, plain
summary: The possessive 'titled house name, first name or my' text, without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House/first name, my, regnal plain
summary: The possessive 'titled house name, first name or my' text, without a tooltip and with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House/first name, my, regnal
summary: The possessive 'titled house name, first name or my' text, with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House or first name possessive, regnal
summary: The possessive 'titled house name or first name' text, with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Titled house or first name, regnal
summary: The character's titled house name or else first name, with a regnal number.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Titles
summary: The list of the character's titles, for a GUI list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source (datamodel) of a list in the map icon layer GUI, so it gives a list of titles. Going by its name, they are the character's own titles.

label: Top liege
summary: The character at the very top of this character's liege chain.
details: Vanilla chains it with GetPrimaryTitle to name the title of that top liege, for example 'county in [title]' in holding texts and raid tooltips.

label: Total income
summary: The character's total income, as a number.
details: Going by its name and its number return type. Vanilla only calls a same-named function on a title in the ledger, which may be another type, so this is a hint.

label: Total merit
summary: The character's total merit, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text field on the main screen (hud.gui). The game documents nothing more about merit here.

label: Total perk points
summary: The character's total perk points, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a number on the main screen. It also shows a part of the main screen and of the character window only when this is above 0 and the character is the local player.

label: Total tax slots
summary: How many tax slots the character has in all, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla writes it after the taxed count as 'taxed/total' on the tax slot button.

label: Trait from group
summary: The character's trait that belongs to the trait group you give.
details: Vanilla passes GetTraitGroup('education_stewardship') or GetTraitGroup('education_martial') and uses the result as the data context of the ledger's education columns. The result is used as an object (a data context), not shown as text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The trait group to look in.
fields.values: a trait group, for example GetTraitGroup('education_martial')

label: Trait group level
summary: The level of the character's trait in the trait group you give, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name and number return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Trait indices
summary: A list of numbers that stand for the character's traits, for a GUI list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list in the multiplayer lobby, so it is a list. Going by its name it holds trait indices.

label: Trait track level
summary: The character's current level on a trait's track, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla passes Trait.Self and TraitLevelTrack.Self and compares the result with a track entry's level to mark the current one. A tooltip shows it as 'Current Level'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The trait that has the track.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The level track of that trait.
fields.values: a trait level track, such as TraitLevelTrack.Self

label: Trait track progress bar
summary: The progress bar data of the character on a trait's track.
details: Vanilla passes Trait.Self and TraitLevelTrack.Self and uses the result as the data context of a bar in the situation list and in tooltips.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The trait that has the track.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The level track of that trait.
fields.values: a trait level track, such as TraitLevelTrack.Self

label: Trait track experience
summary: The experience the character has on a trait's track, as a number.
details: Going by its name and number return type. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The trait that has the track.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The level track of that trait.

label: Traits for character
summary: The list of traits shown for the character, for a GUI list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of a list in the situation list window. Going by its name it holds the character's traits.

label: Travel leader cost
summary: The salary the character costs when a travel starts, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'Salary when a travel starts' for a court position and in the travel planner.

label: Travel leader cost breakdown
summary: A tooltip text explaining how the travel leader cost is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the court position appointment window and the travel planner.

label: Travel plan
summary: The character's current travel plan.
details: Vanilla chains it with GetData, GetNextDestination or GetActivity to name where the character is traveling and which activity the travel belongs to. It returns an object, not text.

label: Travel safety aptitude
summary: The character's travel safety aptitude, as a number.
details: Going by its name, it rates the character for the safety of a travel. Vanilla shows it in the court position appointment window, with negative values cut to 0.

label: Travel safety aptitude breakdown
summary: A tooltip text explaining how the travel safety aptitude is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the court position appointment window.

label: Travel speed aptitude
summary: The character's travel speed aptitude, as a number.
details: Going by its name, it rates the character for the speed of a travel. Vanilla shows it in the court position appointment window, with negative values cut to 0.

label: Travel speed aptitude breakdown
summary: A tooltip text explaining how the travel speed aptitude is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the court position appointment window.

label: Treasury
summary: The gold in the character's treasury, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'Treasury' in the character window and the treasury budget window, and shows the field only when it is 0 or more.

label: Treasury balance
summary: The character's treasury balance, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the ledger with a plus or minus sign, so it can be negative. The game does not say how it differs from GetTreasury.

label: Treasury debt modifier text
summary: Text describing the modifiers that apply while the character is in treasury debt.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla only has a same-named call in a message about being in treasury debt, and the type it is called on is not shown. No game text or GUI line uses it as a character function.

label: Treasury or gold prefix
summary: A short text put before an amount in the texts of the 'add treasury or gold' effect.
details: Vanilla writes it right before the value ('You gain [prefix][amount]'). Going by the name, it marks whether the amount goes to the treasury or to gold; what the prefix is (an icon, a word) is not shown.

label: Treasury tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the character's treasury and its balance.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the treasury display in the character window and the ledger.

label: Tributaries
summary: The list of the character's tributaries, for a GUI list.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla only calls a same-named function on the realm window, which is another type, so this is a hint.

label: Tributary contract
summary: The tributary contract of the character.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the character window and the portraits, and chains GetPortraitIconSmall to get an icon for it.

label: Truce end date
summary: The date a truce of the character ends, for the one you give.
details: Going by its name, its argument and its Date return type. Vanilla never uses it. What the argument must be is not documented (probably the other party).

label: First name only
summary: The character's first name for the interface.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses this exact form. The game documents nothing more.

label: First name only, no format
summary: The character's first name for the interface, without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only ('NoFormat'). Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, no tooltip
summary: The character's first name for the interface, without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only ('NoTooltip'). Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, plain
summary: The character's first name for the interface, without tooltip and without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, not me
summary: The character's first name for the interface, with the 'NotMe' behavior.
details: Going by its name only. What 'NotMe' changes is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name, not me, unformatted
summary: The 'first name only, not me' text without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name, not me, no tooltip
summary: The 'first name only, not me' text without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, not me, plain
summary: The 'first name only, not me' text without tooltip and without text formatting.
details: Vanilla has one line with this name on a character stored in a scope (new_head), where it adds '-ryu' to build a Japanese house name. That line uses another type, so it is a hint.

label: First name only, possessive
summary: The character's first name in the possessive form, for the interface.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, possessive, no format
summary: The possessive first name without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, possessive, no tooltip
summary: The possessive first name without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, possessive, plain
summary: The possessive first name without tooltip and without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name only, possessive, not my
summary: The possessive first name with the 'NotMy' behavior.
details: Going by its name only. What 'NotMy' changes is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name possessive, not my, unformatted
summary: The 'possessive first name, not my' text without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name possessive, not-my, bare
summary: The 'possessive first name, not my' text without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: First name possessive, not my, plain
summary: The 'possessive first name, not my' text without tooltip and text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name
summary: The character's name as the interface shows it.
details: Vanilla uses it very often in texts ('Hire [name] as a tax collector', '[name] is dead'). Going by their names, the NoTooltip and NoFormat variants leave out the tooltip and the text formatting.

label: Name and dynasty
summary: The character's name together with the dynasty, for the interface.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses this exact form.

label: Name and dynasty, no format
summary: The name and dynasty text without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

summary: The name and dynasty text without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

summary: The name and dynasty text without tooltip and text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name and dynasty, not me
summary: The name and dynasty text with the 'NotMe' behavior.
details: Going by its name only. What 'NotMe' changes is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name and dynasty, not me, unformatted
summary: The 'name and dynasty, not me' text without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name and dynasty not-me, bare
summary: The 'name and dynasty, not me' text without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

summary: The 'name and dynasty, not me' text without tooltip and text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

summary: The name and dynasty text in the possessive form.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

summary: The possessive name and dynasty text without a tooltip.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

details: Going by its name only. What 'NotMy' changes is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

summary: The 'possessive name and dynasty, not my' text without tooltip and text formatting.

label: Name, no format
summary: The character's interface name without text formatting.
details: Going by its name and the plain GetUIName it matches. Vanilla never uses this form.

label: Name, no tooltip
summary: The character's interface name without the hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as 'Effects on [name]' and in an invitation signature.

label: Name, plain
summary: The character's interface name without tooltip and without text formatting.
details: Vanilla uses it once, as a text in the great steppe window.

label: Name, not me
summary: The character's interface name, with the 'NotMe' behavior.
details: Vanilla uses it in tooltips such as the hostage and incapable tooltips ('[name] is currently held hostage ...'). What exactly 'NotMe' changes is not documented, though it is probably the name where the viewer is not the character.

label: Name, not me, no format
summary: The 'name, not me' text without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name, not me, no tooltip

details: Vanilla uses it for the name in the character window header and its tooltip. What 'NotMe' changes is not documented.

summary: The 'name, not me' text without tooltip and text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name, possessive
summary: The character's interface name in the possessive form (as in 'Karl's').
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as 'might join the war on [name's] side'.

label: Name, possessive, no format
summary: The possessive name without text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Possessive name, no tooltip
summary: The character's name as shown in the interface, in the possessive form, without a hover tooltip.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla uses it in messages about vassal contract obligations: '[name's] ... obligation has been invalidated'.

label: Name, possessive, plain
summary: The possessive name without tooltip and text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name, possessive, not my, plain
summary: The 'possessive name, not my' text without tooltip and text formatting.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Unassigned vassals
summary: How many of the character's vassals are not assigned to a tax slot, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla writes it in a warning ('You have N unassigned vassals') and tests it for being above 0 in a visibility check on the main screen.

label: Unlanded title
summary: An unlanded title of the character, going by its name.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Unlanded title, skipping player
summary: An unlanded title of the character, with the 'SkipPlayer' behavior.
details: Going by its name only. What 'SkipPlayer' changes is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Unraised knights breakdown
summary: A text breaking down the character's unraised knights, going by its name.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla only has a same-named call on the player in the rally point window's knight tooltip, so this is a hint.

label: Unraised knights
summary: The number of the character's knights that are not raised, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Untaxed jurisdictions
summary: How many of the character's jurisdictions are not taxed, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla writes it in a warning ('You have N untaxed jurisdictions') and tests it for being above 0 in a visibility check on the main screen.

label: Variables description
summary: A text describing the character's variables.
details: Vanilla uses it once, in a debug tooltip that lists AI values. Going by its name it describes the variables stored on the character.

label: Vassal contract
summary: The character's vassal contract.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the vassal detail window and checks IsRightfulLiege on it in the multiplayer lobby.

label: Vassal info text
summary: Information text about the character as a vassal.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Vassal limit
summary: How many direct vassals the character can have before going over the limit, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla compares it with the number of vassals counted towards the limit in the realm window.

label: Vassal limit breakdown
summary: A text showing how the character's vassal limit is made up.
details: Vanilla shows it at the end of the vassal limit tooltip in the realm window.

label: Vassal limit overrun
summary: How many direct vassals the character has above their limit, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses a same-named call in a message ('You are N direct vassals above ...'), on a scope called actor.

label: Vassal limit tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the character's vassal limit.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the realm window.

label: Vassal stance
summary: The character's vassal stance.
details: Vanilla chains GetTextIcon and GetName on it to show the stance's icon and name in AI personality tooltips.

label: Vassal stances that prefer
summary: Text naming the vassal stances that prefer the character you give.
details: Going by its name, its argument and text return type. Vanilla only has a same-named call in the realm window's 'Preferred by' line for the heir, called on a character with Character.Self as the argument; the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the stances are asked about; the only use passes the window's character itself.

label: Vassals
summary: The list of the character's vassals, for a GUI list.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla only has a same-named call on the character window, so this is a hint.

label: Warden
summary: The character who holds this character as a hostage, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it in merit examination texts; those lines compare it with other characters. The game documents nothing more.

label: Wife or husband
summary: The word 'wife' or 'husband', matching the character.
details: Vanilla uses it before the character's name in relationship reasons: 'right under the nose of [name's] [wife/husband], [name]'.

label: Woman or man
summary: The word 'woman' or 'man', matching the character.
details: Vanilla uses it in many texts (18 uses), such as nicknames: 'the [Woman/Man] of Glass', 'As a young [woman/man], ...'.

label: Women or men
summary: The word 'women' or 'men', matching the character.
details: Vanilla uses it in attraction texts: '[name] is not attracted to [women/men]', and in a motto.

label: Has active companion AI setting
summary: Whether the given companion AI setting is switched on for the character.
details: Vanilla passes 'raise_armies' on the main screen. The game documents nothing more about the settings.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The companion AI setting to check.
fields.values: a setting name in single quotes, such as 'raise_armies'

label: Has active diarchy
summary: Whether the character has an active diarchy.
details: Going by its name and a same-named check in the character window. It returns true or false.

label: Has activity state
summary: Whether the character's activity is in the given state.
details: Vanilla checks the states 'travel' and 'passive' in the activity window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a state name in single quotes, such as 'travel' or 'passive'

label: Has artifact claims
summary: Whether the character has a claim on any artifact.
details: Vanilla shows an artifact button only for the local player or when the character has artifacts or artifact claims.

label: Has artifacts
summary: Whether the character owns any artifact.
details: Vanilla shows an artifact button only for the local player or when the character has artifacts or artifact claims.

label: Has at most one spouse
summary: Whether the character has no more than one spouse, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more, and not even a return type.

label: Has barter goods
summary: Whether the character has barter goods.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the character window only when it is true.

label: Has claim on title
summary: Whether the character has a claim on the given title.
details: Vanilla only has same-named calls, on the player (GetPlayer) in interaction buttons and the title window, together with the 'pressed claim' check, with Title.Self as the title.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The title to check the claim on.

label: Has companion AI
summary: Whether the character has the companion AI (automation helper) active.
details: Vanilla only has same-named calls on the player (GetPlayer), to choose between two tooltip texts of the automation toggle and to show a part of the army automation window.

label: Has completed an inspiration
summary: Whether the character has completed an inspiration.
details: Vanilla shows a portrait mark when this is true and the character has no new inspiration; having an inspiration takes priority.

label: Has councillor
summary: Whether the character has a councillor, narrowed by an argument the game does not document.
details: Going by its name and its argument. Vanilla only has a same-named check on a council task, which is another type; what the argument is, is not shown.

label: Has councillor with task in
summary: Whether the character has a councillor doing the given task in the given place.
details: Vanilla uses it on the player with 'task_fabricate_claim' and a county's capital province. The arguments are read from that one use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a task key in single quotes, such as 'task_fabricate_claim'

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The place the task is in; the only use passes a county's capital.

label: Has custom fallback succession
summary: Whether the character's realm has a custom fallback succession.
details: Vanilla uses it in the succession tooltips to add an extra line.

label: Has default companion AI settings
summary: Whether the character's companion AI settings are all at their defaults.
details: Going by its name; vanilla only has a same-named call on the player in the automation tooltip.

label: Has difficulty info
summary: Whether difficulty information exists for the character.
details: Vanilla uses it in the multiplayer lobby to show a part of the screen only when it is true.

label: Has provinces for men-at-arms origin
summary: Whether the character has domain provinces that can be the origin of a men-at-arms regiment.
details: Vanilla uses a same-named call on the player in the military window, only when a regiment has no valid origin province.

label: Has domicile
summary: Whether the character has a domicile.
details: Vanilla uses it with administrative governments in the multiplayer lobby and with house aspirations in the dynasty house window.

label: Has dormant royal court
summary: Whether the character has a royal court that is dormant, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has dynasty
summary: Whether the character belongs to a dynasty.
details: Vanilla uses it to show dynasty parts in the multiplayer lobby and the ledger only when true.

label: Has free accolade slots
summary: Whether the character has a free slot for an accolade.
details: Vanilla uses a same-named call in the knights window to show the choice of acclaimed knights only when there is a free slot.

label: Has guardian
summary: Whether the character has a guardian.
details: Vanilla uses it with an 'is not an adult' check to find children without a guardian.

label: Has infection
summary: Whether the character has the given infection.
details: Vanilla only has a same-named call on the player with Epidemic.Self in a tooltip, so the argument is read from that.

label: Has inspiration
summary: Whether the character has an inspiration.
details: Vanilla uses it to show an inspiration mark on portraits.

label: Has involved migration situation
summary: Whether the character is involved in a migration situation.
details: Vanilla uses it to show and enable parts of the migration window.

label: Has kills known to
summary: Whether the character has kills that are known to the given character.
details: Vanilla passes GetPlayer in the character window to show a kills part only when it is true.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who must know of the kills.

label: Has landed title
summary: Whether the character holds the given landed title.
details: Going by its name and its argument. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Has landed title by key
summary: Whether the character holds the landed title with the given key.
details: Going by its name and its argument. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Has landed titles
summary: Whether the character holds any landed title.
details: Vanilla uses it in the outliner to show different parts for landed and landless characters.

label: Has lessee approval
summary: Whether the character has the approval of the given lessee, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has liege
summary: Whether the character has a liege.
details: Vanilla uses it in a check on whether the character is landless and without a liege.

label: Has merit
summary: Whether the character has merit.
details: Vanilla uses it to show merit parts on the main screen and in the vassal detail window only when true.

label: Has multiple spouses
summary: Whether the character has more than one spouse, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more, and not even a return type.

label: Has new appointment cooldown
summary: Whether the character is in a cooldown before making a new appointment.
details: Vanilla uses it in the government administration window to switch between the appointment parts.

label: Has obscured text
summary: Whether the character has obscured text, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the shared tooltip layout to show a part only when true. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has overlord
summary: Whether the character has an overlord.
details: Vanilla uses it in the realm window to show different parts with and without an overlord.

label: Has perk
summary: Whether the character has the given perk.
details: Vanilla passes Perk.Self in the lifestyle window to show buttons for perks the local player does not yet have.

label: Has potential acclaimed knights
summary: Whether the character has knights who could become acclaimed, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Has pressed claim on title
summary: Whether the character has pressed their claim on the given title.
details: Vanilla uses a same-named call on the player in interaction buttons with Title.Self.

label: Has puppet type
summary: Whether the character is a puppet of the given type, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Puppet type description
summary: A description text for the given puppet type, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it. It returns text.
